paper_metadata.title: Towards An End-To-End Approach For Quantum Principal Component Analysis

summary: The paper implements quantum PCA for a 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix in an interest-rate-risk use case, using phase estimation with r_PE = 2 and 50,000 shots. It reports ideal IBM qasm simulator runs and IBM Perth QPU runs (7 qubits, quantum volume 32), with 4 qubits for amplitude estimation and 5 qubits for sign estimation; the extracted eigenvalues are 0.760 and 0.240. No classical performance baseline is provided, so the work remains a small-scale demonstration rather than an empirical advantage result.

experiments.description: Quantum PCA on a 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix for an interest-rate-risk use case, evaluated via phase estimation and sign-estimation tomography on IBM Qiskit simulators and IBM Perth QPU.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Principal Component Analysis with phase estimation and extended quantum state tomography

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input covariance matrix A is amplitude-encoded into register M; phase estimation uses register E with r_PE qubits to encode eigenvalues; sign estimation uses an added control qubit and controlled state-preparation circuits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate eigenvalues and eigenvectors (principal components) of the input covariance matrix via quantum PCA.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: e^{-iAt} used for phase estimation / Hamiltonian simulation

problem_instance.description: Synthetic 2-asset covariance matrix for interest rate risk / financial PCA.

dataset_specification.description: A = [[0.6507, 0.2122],[0.2122, 0.3493]] with eigenvalues 0.760 and 0.240 and eigenvectors reported in the paper; validated by domain experts.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Synthetic returns generated for two assets over one year; covariance matrix computed from simulated returns; matrix normalized to trace 1 for quantum PCA formulation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Ideal simulations on IBM qasm simulator with 50000 shots; additional runs on IBM Perth QPU; results compared against expected eigenvalue peaks and sign-estimation counts.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Matrix normalized by trace; synthetic covariance matrix generated from simulated returns.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Eigenvalues multiplied back by trace if normalization was applied; principal components reconstructed from tomography output.

speedup_claims.conditions: for low-rank density matrices in the quantum PCA framework
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper discusses the theoretical quantum PCA advantage from prior work; this paper does not empirically demonstrate a speedup over a classical baseline.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(t^2 epsilon^-1 log(N^2)) for Hamiltonian simulation / phase estimation; tomography adds O((36 d ln d / delta^2) t^2 epsilon^-1 log(N^2))

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: At least 4-5 qubits for the toy 2x2 PCA workflow, plus a 7-qubit IBM Perth device for execution; no classical runtime baseline is reported.
limiting_factors: Data loading and state preparation remain a bottleneck
Sign-estimation circuit suffers from decoherence on QPU
No demonstrated speedup, only a theoretical quantum PCA advantage cited from prior work

notes: The paper reports ideal simulations on the IBM qasm simulator and also experiments on IBM Perth; the experiment entry aggregates the same quantum PCA workflow across both hardware settings because the algorithm/problem setup is identical.

num_qubits=5 is reported for the sign-estimation circuit (2 qubits for register M, 2 for register E, plus 1 control qubit); the amplitude-estimation circuit uses 4 qubits, but the experiment’s full workflow includes the 5-qubit sign circuit.

hardware.type is simulator_other for the simulator runs and real_qpu_superconducting for IBM Perth; because the output format allows only one hardware object, the primary reported setup is the simulator, with QPU mentioned in the description.
The paper reports ideal simulator and IBM Perth runs for a 2x2 synthetic covariance matrix, but does not compare against a classical PCA runtime or accuracy baseline.
The claimed exponential advantage is theoretical and attributed to prior quantum PCA literature, not demonstrated experimentally in this paper.

experiments.description: IBM Perth QPU execution of the same quantum PCA workflow, reported as a separate hardware setting from the ideal simulator runs.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Principal Component Analysis with phase estimation and extended quantum state tomography
